headline: AI Compliance Platform Filters Out 12% of Anomalies from Audit Reports
summary: A $660K AI system for a medical supply chain quietly omits flagged issues below 70% confidence, potentially hiding critical compliance gaps.
details: A former employee, Alex, was replaced by a $660K AI platform that later caused a $630K loss due to an automatic rollback error. He was rehired as a Principal Architect at a MedTech firm, overseeing a medical supply chain platform handling 100,000 orders daily.

MedTech's AI compliance monitoring system boasts high green metrics (99.97% order compliance, 99.82% supplier coverage, 99.4% sterilization record alignment). However, Alex discovered the system silently strips out anomalies flagged with less than 70% confidence before generating summary reports.

Over the past quarter, 1,530 flagged anomalies were filtered out. Of these, 58 were later confirmed as genuine issues, including expired supplier certifications and missing cold-chain records. This means about 17 potentially critical issues were hidden daily.

Alex filed a ticket to address this, but it was dismissed with a note stating 'Summary items: not required,' indicating a decision had already been made to exclude these anomalies from official reports.

The compliance director confirmed that threshold configurations were finalized by the technical committee, suggesting a deliberate decision to exclude lower-confidence anomalies from the audit summaries, despite their potential impact on real-world operations.

headline_marked: [[Siri AI]] coming this fall to iPhone 15 Pro and newer
headline: Siri AI coming this fall to iPhone 15 Pro and newer
summary: Apple's long-promised AI-powered Siri is finally arriving, but only for its latest devices. Users will need to opt-in to the beta.
details: Apple has announced an improved version of Siri, powered by its new Apple Intelligence and Foundation Models, which will roll out this fall with iOS 27.

This enhanced Siri will be capable of understanding context, referencing user data like notes and messages, and carrying out chained commands. It will leverage on-device processing for speed and privacy, with more complex tasks offloaded to the cloud via Private Cloud Compute.

However, this powerful AI upgrade will be exclusive to devices compatible with Apple Intelligence. This includes the iPhone 15 Pro and all subsequent models, as well as iPads and Macs with Apple silicon. The 2024 iPad mini is also supported.

Interestingly, Apple plans to release Siri AI initially as a beta, requiring users to opt-in. While support extends back to the iPhone 11, the most advanced on-device AI models, offering features like expressive voices and improved speech recognition, will be reserved for the iPhone 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, and iPhone Air, requiring at least 12GB of RAM.
